title: Fushimi Inari Taisha
description: Thousands of iconic vermilion torii gates winding up a forested mountain. One of Kyoto's most visited and photographed shrines.

title: Kiyomizu-dera
description: UNESCO World Heritage Buddhist temple perched on a hillside with a famous wooden stage overlooking the city of Kyoto.

title: Osaka Castle
description: Magnificent 16th-century castle surrounded by a moat and beautiful park. Features a museum inside with samurai history.

title: Dotonbori
description: Osaka's most famous entertainment district, packed with neon signs, street food, and the iconic Glico running man billboard.

title: Nara Park & Todai-ji
description: Wander freely among friendly deer roaming the park. Todai-ji's Great Buddha Hall is Japan's largest wooden building.

title: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
description: Walk through a towering bamboo forest in western Kyoto. Nearby Tenryu-ji garden and the monkey park are also worth visiting.

title: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
description: Breathtaking Zen temple whose top two floors are covered in gold leaf, perfectly reflected in the surrounding pond.

title: Umeda Sky Building
description: Futuristic twin-tower skyscraper with a "Floating Garden" rooftop observatory offering 360° views of Osaka.

title: Universal Studios Japan
title_ja: ユニバーサル・スタジオ・ジャパン
description: World-class theme park featuring Harry Potter, Super Nintendo World, Minions, and much more — great for a full day out.

title: Kobe Harborland
description: Vibrant waterfront district in Kobe with shopping, restaurants, and beautiful views of the harbour and Rokko mountains.

title: Himeji Castle
description: Japan's finest surviving feudal castle, a UNESCO World Heritage Site known as the White Heron Castle for its dazzling white exterior.

title: Nishiki Market
description: Kyoto's famous narrow covered market street — "Kyoto's Kitchen" — lined with over 100 stalls selling pickles, tofu, sweets, and fresh food.

title: Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan
description: One of the world's largest aquariums, home to whale sharks, manta rays, and sea otters displayed in spectacular cylindrical tanks.

title: Philosopher's Path (Kyoto)
description: A peaceful stone path following a canal lined with hundreds of cherry trees — stunning in spring and serene year-round.

title: Kuromon Market Osaka
description: Osaka's kitchen market: fresh seafood, grilled skewers, and local produce eaten straight from the stalls. Lively and authentic.

title: Arima Onsen
description: One of Japan's oldest hot spring towns, nestled in the Rokko mountains near Kobe — perfect for a day trip and relaxation.

title: Kyoto Imperial Palace
description: The historic residence of Japan's imperial family, surrounded by a beautiful public park popular for picnics and morning runs.

title: Gion District
description: Kyoto's famous geisha district with traditional machiya townhouses, teahouses, and the iconic Hanamikoji Street.

title: Hikone Castle
description: One of Japan's best-preserved original castles, overlooking Lake Biwa. Surrounded by beautiful gardens and a moat.

title: Tenjinbashisuji Shopping Street
description: Japan's longest shopping arcade stretching 2.6km through Osaka — affordable food, local shops, and everyday Osaka life.
